name: Jeim Vincent Ushiyama
bio: Spearheaded the development of a region-aware Video Frame Interpolation framework for anime production, extending AnimeInterp with ROI-guided prioritization and deformable convolutions. His work spans the full project, from model design to the public-facing research platform.
contributions: Designed and implemented the ROI detection mechanism, which fuses Gabor texture analysis and optical flow magnitude into a single attention map.
Architected the web UI & evaluation benchmark dashboards

name: Luke Alexander Pons
bio: Directed the system architecture of an enhanced animation frame interpolation model built upon Deformable Convolutional Neural Networks and Region of Interest maps.
contributions: Implemented the feature extraction and flow estimation components using Python and PyTorch.
Deployed model training on Google Cloud with checkpoint saving and resumability to mitigate virtual machine interruptions.
Containerized the training pipeline using Docker to ensure reproducibility across different machines.

name: Kerr Matthew Nallos
bio: Contributed to the development of a model for automated anime in-betweening, with an emphasis on improving motion interpolation accuracy.
contributions: Implemented the Flow Estimation module of the model.
Investigated RoI-guided approaches to address the limitations of kernel-based video frame interpolation methods.

name: Will Andrew Mercado
bio: Implemented the model's synthesis components and established the evaluation framework used to validate output quality.
contributions: Implemented DCNv2, Laplacian blending, and flow scaling within the synthesis module.
Selected and implemented the evaluation metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and Chamfer Distance) to assess model performance.
